proposed_fix.description: Confirm socket/connection buildup on cartservice pods, then relieve it with a gated, reversible restart or scale-out while investigating the connection leak.
steps: Inspect cartservice pods' open socket counts and states (e.g. ss -s / ss -tan in the pod, or the cartservice_socket metric per pod) to see whether sockets are in ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT or CLOSE_WAIT.
Check cartservice's connections to its backing store (e.g. Redis) and to frontend callers for leaks, missing client reuse or missing timeouts and connection pool limits.
If a single pod is clearly saturated, request human approval to restart that pod (rolling, one at a time) to release leaked sockets.
If load rather than a leak explains the growth, request approval to scale cartservice replicas up by a small number to spread connections.
Watch cartservice_socket, cartservice error rate and frontend-external_error after each change before continuing.
If a leak is confirmed, open a ticket for a code or config fix (connection reuse, pool size, timeouts).
preconditions: Confirm the cartservice_socket deviation (E7) and cartservice error rate (E2) are still present in current data.
Confirm the node's conntrack usage and NIC receive errors are not the actual bottleneck, since the runbooks are node-level and unverified here.
Ensure there are enough healthy replicas that restarting one pod will not cause an outage.
Get on-call approval before any restart or scale change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Scale cartservice replicas back to the original count; a restarted pod is replaced automatically by the deployment, and if a config change was made, revert it to the previous version.
